content.comment_body: I'm setting up a [product_name] with [version_no] and programming using [product_name] [version_no]. After I power off, the newly loaded program gets deleted, and the previous program appears instead.
Do you have an mSD card inserted in the [product_name], and is the previous program stored on it?
Are you certain? As far as I know, that's the only possible explanation. With each reboot, the [product_name] loads the program from the mSD card if one is present.

I'm developing with [product_name] [version_no], but I choose [version_no] to download the program. I heard that programming with [product_name] [version_no] is necessary for proper saving. If I remove the mSD card, can I load programs normally?

1) A program in the [product_name] is saved to flash memory and should stay after a power outage. It can only be deleted intentionally, for example, using [product_name] or by transferring a new program. 2) Even in case of malfunction, the origin of the old program needs clarification, as only one program can be stored at a time. 3) What you describe most likely happens if the old program is saved on an SD card. 4) Once the mSD card is removed from the [product_name], what you described should no longer happen.

analysis.insight_summary: New programs loaded onto the [product_name] are deleted upon reboot and the previous program is restored, unless the microSD card is removed. Users highlight a possible issue related to firmware behavior, memory retention, or version compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the newly loaded program in the [product_name] to persist after power-off, without reverting to the old program.
